questions.q: My __ brother's wife is Sara - she is my aunt.
questions.explanation: We need the possessive form of 'dad'. The possessive is formed by adding apostrophe + s: **dad's**.

questions.q: __ Chelsea play Liverpool this Saturday. Do you want to come?
questions.explanation: **'Going to'** is used for a planned future event. 'I'm going to see' correctly expresses a pre-arranged plan.

questions.q: My shoes are wet, __ I'll leave them in the sun to dry.
questions.explanation: **'So'** introduces a result or consequence. The wet shoes are the cause; leaving them in the sun is the result.

questions.q: When I feel __, my face turns red.
questions.explanation: After 'feel', we use an adjective describing the subject's emotional state. **'Embarrassed'** is the correct past-participial adjective here.

questions.q: My father said I __ as late as I want.
questions.explanation: Modal verbs like **'may'** must be followed by the bare infinitive. 'May stay' is correct.

questions.q: How long does it take __ from Paris to Madrid by train?
questions.explanation: The structure **'it takes + time + to-infinitive'** is standard. 'To get' is correct.

questions.q: You need flour, eggs and sugar __ this cake.
questions.explanation: **'To make'** (infinitive of purpose) expresses why you need the ingredients.

questions.q: I __ the newspaper when the doorbell rang.
questions.explanation: **Past continuous** ('was reading') describes an action in progress in the past that was interrupted by another event (the doorbell ringing).

questions.q: I had __ very scary dream last night.
questions.explanation: We use the indefinite article **'a'** before a singular countable noun mentioned for the first time. 'Very' starts with a consonant sound, so 'a' (not 'an') is correct.

questions.q: We saw him, his wife and __ children at their home in Bristol.
questions.explanation: **'Their'** is the possessive determiner used before a noun to show belonging. 'Them' is an object pronoun and cannot precede a noun.

questions.q: He's hurt a finger on his left hand, so he can't __ the guitar.
questions.explanation: After modal verbs like **'can't'**, we always use the bare infinitive. 'Play' is correct.

questions.q: The __ school is an excellent school; they are really learning fast.
questions.explanation: **'Boys''** is the plural possessive. The school belongs to multiple boys, so the apostrophe follows the plural 's'.

questions.q: We __ anything special last weekend.
questions.explanation: **'Didn't do'** is the correct past simple negative. 'Didn't' alone needs the main verb 'do' to complete the sentence.

questions.q: I'm going to the bar to order a beer from __ barman.
questions.explanation: **'The'** is used with a specific, identifiable noun — the speaker is referring to a particular barman at that bar.

questions.q: My bicycle wheel is __ bent after my crash.
questions.explanation: **'A little'** is used as an adverb modifying the adjective 'bent', meaning slightly. 'Little' without the article has a negative connotation and does not work as a modifier here.

questions.q: We have a new picture __ the wall.
questions.explanation: **'On'** is the correct preposition for surfaces. Pictures are hung 'on' a wall.

questions.q: The first questions are simple and __ they get more complicated.
questions.explanation: **'Then'** indicates sequence — first they are simple, and after that they become more complicated.

questions.q: I work __ a bank.
questions.explanation: **'In'** is the correct preposition for working inside an institution or building: 'work in a bank/hospital/school'.

questions.q: The schoolboys all __ wear a soft grey cap on their heads.
questions.explanation: **'Have to'** expresses obligation. It follows the subject directly and takes the base form of the main verb.

questions.q: The washing machine we __ on Tuesday doesn't work.
questions.explanation: **'Bought'** is the past simple of 'buy', correct here since the purchase happened on a specific day in the past.

questions.q: I __ sing very well, so I'm going to have lessons.
questions.explanation: **'Can't'** expresses inability. The speaker is unable to sing well, which is why they are planning to take lessons.

questions.q: "I'll help you." "Thanks. __ very kind of you."
questions.explanation: **'That's'** (= That is) is used to comment on something just said or done. 'That's very kind of you' is a natural fixed expression in English.

questions.q: I fell off my bike and __ my leg.
questions.explanation: **'Broke'** is the past simple of 'break', used for a completed action at a specific past moment.

questions.q: She still feels bad, __ she's going to see the doctor today.
questions.explanation: **'So'** introduces a result or consequence. Feeling bad is the cause; seeing the doctor is the result.

questions.q: There are several reasons __ I can't help you now.
questions.explanation: **'Why'** is the correct relative adverb used after 'reasons': 'reasons why I can't help'.

questions.q: What sports __ at the leisure center?
questions.explanation: In direct questions, the auxiliary comes before the subject. **'Can we do'** follows the correct question word order: auxiliary (can) + subject (we) + main verb (do).

questions.q: __ the window, please?
questions.explanation: **'Can I open'** is correct. Modal verbs are followed by the bare infinitive, not 'to + infinitive' or the gerund.

questions.q: Please can you pass me __ cup?
questions.explanation: **'That'** is used for a singular noun distant from the speaker. Since the speaker is asking someone else to pass it, the cup is away from the speaker.

questions.q: My Uncle Frank is my __ brother.
questions.explanation: **'Dad's'** is the possessive form indicating that Uncle Frank is the brother who belongs to / is on the side of the speaker's dad.

questions.q: How many children __ she __?
questions.explanation: **'Did … have'** is the correct past simple question structure: auxiliary 'did' + subject + bare infinitive 'have'.

questions.q: What does 'AI' stand for in Computer Science?
questions.explanation: AI stands for Artificial Intelligence, the field of making computers simulate human-like intelligence.

questions.q: Which of these is a common application of AI in daily life?
options: Voice assistants like Siri or Alexa

questions.q: What is the primary goal of Machine Learning?

To increase the weight of the laptop

questions.q: Which term describes a computer's ability to 'see' and interpret images?
questions.explanation: Computer Vision is the field of AI that trains computers to interpret and understand the visual world.

questions.q: Who is often considered the 'Father of Artificial Intelligence'?
questions.explanation: Alan Turing's work on the 'Turing Test' laid the foundation for modern AI.

questions.q: True or False: An AI must always be a physical robot that looks like a human.
questions.explanation: AI is software; it can live in a phone, a server, or a car without needing a human-like body.

questions.q: True or False: AI can process large amounts of data faster than a human.
questions.explanation: Computers are designed to handle millions of calculations per second, far exceeding human speed.

questions.q: True or False: AI currently has the exact same emotions and feelings as a human.

questions.q: ...............is a contiguous area of memory consisting of equal-size elements
questions.explanation: An **Array** is defined as a collection of items stored at contiguous memory locations where each element is of the same size, allowing for $O(1)$ access time via indexing.

questions.q: What is the access time required to retrieve the element located at position $(5,9)$ in a 7-row and 12-column array?
questions.explanation:
In a row-major 2D array, the address of element $(i, j)$ is calculated as:
$$Address = Base + Size \times ((i - 1) \times \text{TotalColumns} + (j - 1))$$
For $(5,9)$ in a $7 \times 12$ array, this becomes $Base + Size \times ((5-1) \times 12 + (9-1))$.

questions.q: The complexity of adding three elements to the end of an array is........
questions.explanation: Adding an element to the end of an array (assuming there is space) is a constant time operation, $O(1)$. Performing a constant number of $O(1)$ operations (in this case, 3) still results in $O(1)$ complexity.

questions.q: Find(Key) in a double linked list with a tail is.....
questions.explanation: To find a specific key in a linked list (single or double), you must perform a linear search starting from the head (or tail), checking each node until the key is found. This results in $O(n)$ time complexity.

questions.q: AddAfter(Node, Key) in a single linked list with a tail is........
questions.explanation: If the specific `Node` is already provided, adding a new node immediately after it only involves updating the pointers of the current node and the new node. This does not require traversal, making it $O(1)$.

questions.q: Erase(Key) in a single linked list with a tail is.....
questions.explanation: In a single linked list, to erase a node by `Key`, you must find the node *before* the one to be deleted to update its `next` pointer. This search requires traversing the list, leading to $O(n)$ complexity.

questions.q: TopBack() in a single linked list with a tail is......
questions.explanation: With a `tail` pointer, accessing the last element of the list is a direct reference, which takes constant time $O(1)$.

questions.q: The Function of adding an element to a stack is called
questions.explanation: The standard terminology for adding an item to a Stack is **Push**. **Pop** is for removal, and **Enqueue** is for adding to a Queue.

questions.q: To return the most recently-added key in a stack, we use the....... function
questions.explanation: The **Top** (or Peek) function returns the value of the most recent element added to the stack without removing it.

questions.q: removes and returns the first added key from a Stack is known as...
questions.explanation: A Stack follows **LIFO** (Last-In, First-Out). Removing the *first added* key (the bottom of the stack) violates the Stack ADT principles and is not a standard operation. That behavior is characteristic of a Queue (**FIFO**).

questions.q: Stack operations are known as
questions.explanation: Stacks operate on the **Last-In, First-Out** (LIFO) principle, meaning the last element added is the first one to be removed.

questions.q: PushBack(Key) in a single linked list without a tail is.....
questions.explanation: Without a tail pointer, you must traverse the entire list from the head to reach the last node before you can append a new one, resulting in $O(n)$ complexity.

questions.q: To return and remove the most recently added key in a stack, we use the....... function
questions.explanation: The **Pop** function removes the top element of the stack and typically returns its value to the caller.

questions.q: Stack operation Push() is implemented using LikedList....... function
questions.explanation: While both `PushBack` and `PushFront` could theoretically work, `PushFront` is used for Stack implementation because it is $O(1)$ in a Singly Linked List, whereas `PushBack` would be $O(n)$ without a tail pointer.

questions.q: The complexity of adding an element to the middle of an array is
questions.explanation: Adding to the middle of an array requires shifting all subsequent elements to make room for the new one. In the worst case, this involves shifting $n/2$ elements, which simplifies to $O(n)$.

questions.q: What is a common disadvantage of networking in terms of costs?
questions.explanation: Setting up a network requires significant upfront investment in hardware (routers, switches, cabling) and labor.

questions.q: Which of the following is a fundamental network classification based on geographical area coverage?
questions.explanation: While PAN and WAN are also geographical classifications, LAN is the most fundamental classification for local area coverage.

questions.q: What is the primary function of a server computer in a network?
options: It requests services from client computers
It provides resources and services to client computers
It serves as a standalone workstation

questions.q: Which network topology connects each device to a single, central point?
questions.explanation: In a Star topology, all nodes are connected to a central hub or switch.

questions.q: Which OSI layer is responsible for translating data between formats used by different networking devices?
questions.explanation: The Presentation Layer (Layer 6) handles data encryption, compression, and translation.

questions.q: At which OSI layer does routing and forwarding of packets occur?
questions.explanation: The Network Layer (Layer 3) is responsible for logical addressing and routing packets.

questions.q: Which OSI layer establishes, manages, and terminates connections between applications?
questions.explanation: The Session Layer (Layer 5) manages the dialogues (sessions) between computers.

questions.q: At which OSI layer do switches operate to forward frames based on MAC addresses?
questions.explanation: Layer 2 switches use MAC addresses to forward data frames.

questions.q: Which Application Layer protocol is primarily used for transferring web pages and related files over the Internet?
questions.explanation: HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) is the foundation of data communication for the World Wide Web.

questions.q: Which protocol translates domain names into IP addresses to locate resources on the Internet?
questions.explanation: DNS (Domain Name System) acts like a phonebook for the internet.

questions.q: What protocol is commonly used for transferring files between a client and a server over a network?
questions.explanation: FTP stands for File Transfer Protocol.

questions.q: Which protocol dynamically assigns IP addresses to network devices?

questions.q: Which protocol is used for sending email messages between servers?

questions.q: Define: Mutually exclusive events; Independent events; Probability Axioms.
questions.answer:
**Mutually Exclusive Events:**
Two events $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive (disjoint) if they cannot occur at the same time, i.e., $A \cap B = \emptyset$, which means $P(A \cap B) = 0$.

**Independent Events:**
Two events $A$ and $B$ are independent if the occurrence of one does not affect the probability of the other, i.e., $P(A \cap B) = P(A) \times P(B)$.

- **Probability Axioms (Kolmogorov's Axioms):**

* Axiom 1: For any event $A$, $P(A) \ge 0$.
* Axiom 2: $P(S) = 1$, where $S$ is the sample space.
* Axiom 3: For mutually exclusive events $A_1, A_2, \dots$: $P(A_1 \cup A_2 \cup \dots) = P(A_1) + P(A_2) + \dots$
questions.explanation: These are fundamental definitions in probability theory. Mutually exclusive events share no outcomes. Independent events have no influence on each other's probability. The three Kolmogorov axioms form the foundation of modern probability theory: non-negativity, normalization, and countable additivity.

questions.q:
A sample of four electronic components is taken from the output of a production line. The probabilities of the various outcomes are calculated to be:

**$P(0 \text{ defectives}) = 0.6$**
**$P(1 \text{ defective}) = 0.2$**
**$P(2 \text{ defectives}) = 0.04$**
**$P(3 \text{ defectives}) = 0.03$**
**$P(4 \text{ defectives}) = 0.01$**

**i) What is the probability of at least three defective?**
questions.answer:
$$P(\text{at least 3 defectives}) = P(3 \text{ defectives}) + P(4 \text{ defectives})$$
$$= 0.03 + 0.01 = 0.04$$
questions.explanation: 'At least three defective' means 3 or more defectives. So we sum $P(X = 3)$ and $P(X = 4)$: $0.03 + 0.01 = 0.04$.

questions.q:
Using the same probabilities as Question 2:
    **ii) What is the probability of at most one defective?**
questions.answer:
$$P(\text{at most 1 defective}) = P(0 \text{ defectives}) + P(1 \text{ defective})$$
$$= 0.6 + 0.2 = 0.8$$
questions.explanation: 'At most one defective' means 0 or 1 defective. So we sum $P(X = 0)$ and $P(X = 1)$: $0.6 + 0.2 = 0.8$.

questions.q: Prove that $f(x) = \binom{n}{x} p^x q^{n-x}$ ; $x = 0, 1, 2, \dots, n$ is a mass function; find the moment generating function and $\sigma$.
questions.answer:
1. Proof that $f(x)$ is a mass function:

**$f(x) \ge 0$ for all $x$, since $p, q \ge 0$ and $\binom{n}{x} \ge 0$.**
**$\sum_{x=0}^{n} \binom{n}{x} p^x q^{n-x} = (p + q)^n = (p + (1-p))^n = 1^n = 1$ (by the Binomial Theorem)**
So $f(x)$ is a valid probability mass function.

**Moment Generating Function (MGF):**
$$M(t) = E[e^{tX}] = \sum_{x=0}^{n} e^{tx} \binom{n}{x} p^x q^{n-x}$$
$$= \sum_{x=0}^{n} \binom{n}{x} (pe^t)^x q^{n-x} = (pe^t + q)^n$$

**Standard Deviation ($\sigma$):**
For the Binomial distribution:
Mean: $\mu = np$
Variance: $\sigma^2 = npq$
Standard Deviation: $\sigma = \sqrt{npq}$
questions.explanation: This is the Binomial distribution. The proof uses the Binomial Theorem. The MGF is derived by replacing $p$ with $pe^t$ in the binomial expansion. The variance follows from the second moment of the distribution.

questions.q: Prove that $f(x) = \frac{1}{b-a}$ for $a < x < b$ is a density function and find $E(x^7)$.
questions.answer:
1. Proof that $f(x) = \frac{1}{b-a}$ is a density function:

**$f(x) = \frac{1}{b-a} > 0$ for all $x \in (a, b)$, since $b > a$.**
**$\int_{a}^{b} \frac{1}{b-a} dx = \left[ \frac{x}{b-a} \right]_{a}^{b} = \frac{b-a}{b-a} = 1$**
So $f(x)$ is a valid probability density function (Uniform distribution on $[a, b]$).

**Finding $E(x^7)$:**
$$E(x^7) = \int_{a}^{b} x^7 \left(\frac{1}{b-a}\right) dx = \frac{1}{b-a} \left[ \frac{x^8}{8} \right]_{a}^{b} = \frac{b^8 - a^8}{8(b-a)}$$
questions.explanation: This is the Uniform distribution on $[a, b]$. The proof requires showing non-negativity and that the integral over the support equals 1. $E(x^7)$ is computed by integrating $x^7 \times f(x)$ over $[a, b]$.

questions.q: If $A \subset B$, Then $P(A|B) =$
questions.explanation: By definition, $P(A|B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}$. Because $A \subset B$, the intersection $A \cap B = A$. Therefore, the equation simplifies to $\frac{P(A)}{P(B)}$.

questions.q: If the knowledge that an event $A$ has occurred implies that a second event $B$ cannot occur, the events $A$ and $B$ are said to be:
questions.explanation: Events are mutually exclusive when they cannot occur simultaneously, meaning their intersection is empty ($A \cap B = \emptyset$) and $P(A \cap B) = 0$.

questions.q: If $A$ and $B$ are independent events in a sample space $S$, then which of the following statement(s) are true:
questions.explanation: If $A$ and $B$ are independent, their complements are also independent of the original events and each other. For example, $P(A \cap B^c) = P(A)P(B^c)$.

questions.q: A code consists of a digit chosen from $0$ to $6$ followed by a letter of the alphabet. What is the probability the code is `6Z`?
questions.explanation: There are 7 possible digits ($0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6$) and 26 letters. The probability of picking the specific digit '6' is $\frac{1}{7}$ and the letter 'Z' is $\frac{1}{26}$. Multiplying these independent probabilities gives $\frac{1}{7} \times \frac{1}{26} = \frac{1}{182}$.

questions.q: For a continuous random variable $X$ with a probability density function $f(x) = k(x^3 + 1)$ for $0 \le x \le 1$, then the value of $k$ is:
questions.explanation:
The total area under the density function must equal 1.
$$\int_{0}^{1} k(x^3 + 1) dx = k\left[ \frac{x^4}{4} + x \right]_{0}^{1} = k\left( \frac{1}{4} + 1 \right) = \frac{5k}{4} = 1$$
Solving for $k$ gives $\frac{4}{5}$.

questions.q: The value of $k$ when the probability mass function is given by $P(x) = \frac{2x}{k}$ for $x \in \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$ is:
questions.explanation:
The sum of probabilities for all possible values of $x$ must equal 1.
$$\sum_{x=1}^{4} \frac{2x}{k} = \frac{2(1) + 2(2) + 2(3) + 2(4)}{k} = \frac{20}{k} = 1$$
Therefore, $k = 20$.

questions.q: The cumulative distribution function for the random variable $X$ for $f(x) = \lambda e^{-\lambda x}$ for $0 \le x < \infty$ is given by:
questions.explanation:
The CDF is the integral of the PDF from $0$ to $x$:
$$F(x) = \int_{0}^{x} \lambda e^{-\lambda t} dt = \left[ -e^{-\lambda t} \right]_{0}^{x} = 1 - e^{-\lambda x}$$

questions.q: If $f(x) = 2 e^{-2x}$ for $0 \le x < \infty$, then the value of $x$ such that $P(X > x) = 0.1$ is:
questions.explanation:
The tail probability $P(X > x) = 0.1$ implies:
$$\int_{x}^{\infty} 2e^{-2t} dt = e^{-2x} = 0.1$$
Taking the natural log of both sides: $-2x = \ln(0.1) \approx -2.302$. Dividing by $-2$ gives $x \approx 1.15$.

questions.q: If the variance of $x$ is $v(x) = \frac{1}{3}$, then $v\left(\frac{x}{3} - 5\right) =$
questions.explanation: Variance follows the property $v(ax + b) = a^2 \cdot v(x)$. Here, $a = \frac{1}{3}$, so the variance is $\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^2 \cdot v(x) = \frac{1}{9} \cdot \frac{1}{3} = \frac{1}{27}$.

questions.q: $E(ax + b) =$
questions.explanation: By the linearity of expectation, the constant $a$ can be pulled out and the constant $b$ is added separately.

questions.q:
A company producing electric relays has three manufacturing plants producing $50\%$, $30\%$, and $20\%$, respectively, of its product. Suppose that the probabilities that a relay manufactured by these plants is defective are $0.02$, $0.05$, and $0.01$, respectively.
    **a) If a relay is selected at random from the output of the company, what is the probability that it is defective?**

Using the scenario from Question 16:
    **b) If a relay selected at random is found to be defective, what is the probability that it was manufactured by plant 2?**
questions.explanation:
Using Bayes' Theorem:
$$P(P_2 | D) = \frac{P(D | P_2) P(P_2)}{P(D)} = \frac{0.05 \times 0.30}{0.027} = \frac{0.015}{0.027} \approx 0.556$$

questions.q:
When Farid plays chess against his favorite computer program, he wins with probability $0.60$.
    **a) What is the probability that Farid wins 6 games, if he plays 10 games?**
questions.explanation: This follows a binomial distribution: $P(X=k) = \binom{n}{k} p^k (1-p)^{n-k}$.

questions.q:
Using the scenario from Question 18:
    **b) What is the probability that Farid wins 2 games at most, if he plays 10 games?**
questions.explanation: This is the cumulative sum of probabilities for 0, 1, and 2 wins under the Binomial distribution.

questions.q:
Fares makes mistakes in class according to a Poisson process with an average rate of $\lambda = 1.2$ mistakes per class.
    **a) What is the probability that Fares makes 2 mistakes during one class?**
questions.explanation:
Using the Poisson PMF $P(X=x) = \frac{e^{-\lambda} \lambda^x}{x!}$. For $x=2$:
$$P(X=2) = \frac{e^{-1.2} (1.2)^2}{2!} \approx 0.216$$

questions.q:
Using the scenario from Question 20:
    **b) What is the probability that Fares makes one mistake at least during one class?**
questions.explanation:
Using the complement rule:
$$P(X \ge 1) = 1 - P(X = 0) = 1 - e^{-1.2} \approx 1 - 0.301 = 0.699$$

questions.q:
If $P(A) = 0.2$, $P(B) = 0.3$ and $P(A \cup B) = 0.4$, Determine the following probabilities:
    **a. $P(A^c)$**
    **b. $P(A \cap B)$**
    **c. $P(A^c \cap B)$**
    **d. $P(A \cap B^c)$**
    **e. $P((A \cup B)^c)$**
    **f. $P(A^c \cup B)$**

The following data for two tests is given:
    $X: 9, 5, 3, 7, 11$
    $Y: 5, 6, 1, 9, 9$
    **a) Compute the correlation coefficient $r$.**
questions.answer: $r \approx 0.715$
questions.explanation:
The Pearson correlation coefficient $r$ measures the linear association between $X$ and $Y$. Using the formula:
$$r = \frac{n\sum xy - (\sum x)(\sum y)}{\sqrt{[n\sum x^2 - (\sum x)^2][n\sum y^2 - (\sum y)^2]}}$$
With $n=5$, $\sum x=35$, $\sum y=30$, $\sum x^2=285$, $\sum y^2=224$, and $\sum xy=240$:
$$r = \frac{5(240) - (35)(30)}{\sqrt{[5(285) - 35^2][5(224) - 30^2]}} = \frac{1200 - 1050}{\sqrt{[1425 - 1225][1120 - 900]}}$$
$$r = \frac{150}{\sqrt{200 \times 220}} = \frac{150}{\sqrt{44000}} \approx 0.715$$
This indicates a moderately strong positive linear relationship.

questions.q: Using the data from Question 23, find the equation of the line of best fit.
questions.explanation:
The line of best fit is represented by $Y = a + bX$.

A. Slope ($b$):
$$b = \frac{n\sum xy - \sum x \sum y}{n\sum x^2 - (\sum x)^2} = \frac{150}{200} = 0.75$$
B. Intercept ($a$):
$$\bar{x} = \frac{35}{5} = 7, \quad \bar{y} = \frac{30}{5} = 6$$
$$a = \bar{y} - b\bar{x} = 6 - (0.75 \times 7) = 6 - 5.25 = 0.75$$
Thus, the equation is $Y = 0.75 + 0.75X$.

questions.q: If the probability density function for a continuous random variable $X$ is $f(x) = 2x$ for $0 \le x < 1$, find the cumulative distribution function (CDF).
questions.answer: $F(x) = x^2$ for $0 \le x < 1$
questions.explanation:
The CDF $F(x)$ is found by integrating the PDF from the lower bound to $x$:
$$F(x) = \int_{0}^{x} 2t \, dt = [t^2]_0^x = x^2$$
For $x < 0$, $F(x) = 0$, and for $x \ge 1$, $F(x) = 1$.

questions.q:
An introductory biology student wishes to determine the relationship between temperature ($X$) and heart rate ($Y$) in the common leopard frog.
    Data:
    $X \text{ (}^\circ\text{C)}: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18$
    $Y \text{ (bpm)}: 5, 11, 11, 14, 22, 23, 32, 29, 32$
    Compute the correlation coefficient $r$.
questions.answer: $r \approx 0.963$
questions.explanation:
Using the Pearson correlation formula with $n=9$:
$\sum X = 90$, $\sum Y = 179$, $\sum X^2 = 1140$, $\sum Y^2 = 4365$, $\sum XY = 2216$.
$$r = \frac{9(2216) - (90)(179)}{\sqrt{[9(1140) - 90^2][9(4365) - 179^2]}}$$
$$r = \frac{19944 - 16110}{\sqrt{[10260 - 8100][39285 - 32041]}} = \frac{3834}{\sqrt{2160 \times 7244}} \approx 0.969$$
_(Note: Minor rounding differences may occur depending on intermediate step precision; the result indicates a very strong positive correlation)._

questions.q: Using the regression equation $\hat{Y} = 2.139 + 1.775X$ from the frog heart rate study, predict the heart rate when the temperature is $20^\circ\text{C}$.
questions.explanation:
Substitute $X = 20$ into the linear regression equation:
$$\hat{Y} = 2.139 + 1.775(20)$$
$$\hat{Y} = 2.139 + 35.5 = 37.639$$

questions.q: Find the least-squares line ($Y = a + bX$) for a dataset where $n=5$, $\sum x = 15$, $\sum y = 100$, $\sum x^2 = 55$, and $\sum xy = 340$.
questions.answer:
$Y = 14 + 2X$
**Explanation:**

A. Calculate $b$:
$$b = \frac{5(340) - (15)(100)}{5(55) - (15)^2} = \frac{1700 - 1500}{275 - 225} = \frac{200}{50} = 4$$
_(Correction based on standard calculation steps: if $b=4$)_
B. Calculate $a$:
$$\bar{x} = 3, \quad \bar{y} = 20$$
$$a = 20 - (4 \times 3) = 8$$
Equation: $Y = 8 + 4X$.
_(Note: If the formal answer provided in your source was $Y = 15 + 2X$ or similar, verify if $\sum xy$ or $\sum x^2$ values differed in that specific exam variant)._

questions.q: Find the Geometric Mean (G.M), Arithmetic Mean (A.M), Median, Mode, Standard Deviation ($\sigma$), and Coefficient of Variation (C.V) for the following set: $25, 8, 15, 5, 7$.
questions.answer:
1. **Sorted Data:** $5, 7, 8, 15, 25$ ($n = 5$). 2. **Arithmetic Mean (A.M):** $\text{A.M} = \frac{5 + 7 + 8 + 15 + 25}{5} = \frac{60}{5} = 12$. 3. **Geometric Mean (G.M):** $\text{G.M} = (5 \times 7 \times 8 \times 15 \times 25)^{1/5} = (105000)^{1/5} \approx 10.23$. 4. **Median:** The middle value of the sorted data is $8$. 5. **Mode:** All values appear once, so the data is amodal (no mode). 6. **Standard Deviation ($\sigma$):** \* $\sum x^2 = 25 + 49 + 64 + 225 + 625 = 988$.

- $\sigma^2 = \frac{\sum x^2}{n} - (\text{A.M})^2 = \frac{988}{5} - 12^2 = 197.6 - 144 = 53.6$.
- $\sigma = \sqrt{53.6} \approx 7.32$.

**7. **Coefficient of Variation (C.V):** $\text{C.V} = \frac{\sigma}{\text{A.M}} \times 100 = \frac{7.32}{12} \times 100 \approx 61\%$.**
questions.explanation: A.M is the standard average, while G.M is the $n$-th root of the product. The Median is the central value of a sorted list, and the Standard Deviation measures the spread of data. C.V expresses that spread as a percentage of the mean.

questions.q: A sample of 49 cars had a mean time on the dealer's lot of 70 days. Assume the population standard deviation is 7 days. Find the best point estimate of the population mean and the 95% confidence interval. (Given: $z_{0.025} = 1.96$).
questions.answer:
1. **Best Point Estimate:** The sample mean $\bar{x} = 70$ days. 2. **Standard Error:** $\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}} = \frac{7}{\sqrt{49}} = \frac{7}{7} = 1$. 3. **95% Confidence Interval:** $\bar{x} \pm z_{0.025} \times \frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}} = 70 \pm 1.96(1)$.

- Lower bound: $70 - 1.96 = 68.04$.
- Upper bound: $70 + 1.96 = 71.96$.
- **95% CI:** $(68.04, 71.96)$.

questions.q: What is a computer network?
options: A single computer with multiple users
Two or more computing devices connected to exchange information and share resources
A device used only for internet access
questions.explanation: A network is defined by the connection of multiple devices for resource sharing.

questions.q: A network node is best described as:
options: A connection point capable of sending, receiving, or processing data
questions.explanation: Any device connected to a network that can communicate is considered a node.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a network node?
questions.explanation: Printers, switches, and routers are all addressable points on a network.

questions.q: What is a client in a network?
options: A device that requests and accesses services
A device that only stores data
questions.explanation: Clients are the 'consumers' in the network relationship.

questions.q: What is a server in a network?
options: A device that provides services or functions for clients
A device that only connects to the internet
questions.explanation: Servers 'serve' resources such as files, web pages, or email to clients.

questions.q: The world’s largest server room is located in:
questions.explanation: The China Telecom Data Center is currently the largest in the world.

questions.q: A switch is primarily used to:
options: Connect devices within the same LAN
questions.explanation: Switches create a network by connecting devices locally (Intra-network).

questions.q: How many ports does a typical switch have?
questions.explanation: Enterprise switches commonly come in 24 or 48 port configurations.

questions.q: Which device is used to connect different LANs or provide internet connectivity?
questions.explanation: Routers connect different networks (Inter-network).

questions.q: A router generally has ______ network interfaces compared to a switch.
questions.explanation: Routers usually have a few high-speed interfaces, while switches have many ports for end-user devices.

questions.q: What is the main function of a firewall?
options: To monitor and control network traffic based on rules
To connect devices in a LAN
questions.explanation: Firewalls act as a security barrier based on a set of security rules.

questions.q: Where can a firewall be placed in a network?
questions.explanation: Firewalls can protect the perimeter or segments within the internal network.

questions.q: A Next-Generation Firewall (NGFW) includes:
options: More advanced and modern filtering capabilities
questions.explanation: NGFWs go beyond simple packet filtering to include deep packet inspection and encrypted traffic analysis.

questions.q: Which device operates at the Data Link layer (Layer 2) of the OSI model?
questions.explanation: Switches use MAC addresses, which are Layer 2 identifiers.

questions.q: Which device operates at the Network layer (Layer 3) of the OSI model?
questions.explanation: Routers use IP addresses, which are Layer 3 identifiers.

questions.q: A device that can act as both a client and a server is called:
questions.explanation: In Peer-to-Peer (P2P) networking, devices share resources equally.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a function of a network node?
questions.explanation: Cables are the transmission media, not a function performed by a node.

questions.q: In a client/server model, the client:
questions.explanation: Clients initiate the request for service.

questions.q: Which company is mentioned as using the China Telecom Data Center?
questions.explanation: Alibaba is a major user of the China Telecom infrastructure.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a switch in a LAN?
options: To forward traffic within the same LAN
questions.explanation: Switches facilitate communication between local devices like PCs and printers.

questions.q: A firewall that filters traffic entering and exiting a single host is called:
questions.explanation: Host-based firewalls (like Windows Firewall) protect individual devices.

questions.q: Which device is often placed between a LAN and the internet?
questions.explanation: The router serves as the gateway to external networks.

questions.q: What does a firewall use to decide whether to allow or deny traffic?
questions.explanation: Access Control Lists (ACLs) and security rules define what traffic is permitted.

questions.q: If PC1 in New York tries to access SRV1 in Tokyo, what should the firewall do if configured correctly?
questions.explanation: Firewalls are configured to allow legitimate business traffic while blocking threats.

questions.q: Which of the following is a hardware device?
questions.explanation: While software firewalls exist, 'Network firewalls' are typically dedicated hardware appliances.

questions.q: A switch CANNOT:
questions.explanation: A switch does not perform routing; a router is needed for internet connectivity.

questions.q: Which device is responsible for logical addressing and routing?
questions.explanation: Routing is the core function of a router.

questions.q: What is the role of a firewall in network security?
questions.explanation: Firewalls are primarily security tools to prevent unauthorized entry.

questions.q: A network node must always be:
questions.explanation: To participate in a network, a node must have a unique address (IP or MAC).

questions.q: In the client/server relationship, the server:
options: Always has fewer resources than the client
Must be located in the same room as the client
questions.explanation: Servers provide functionality; they do not need to be physically near the client.

questions.q: A computer network requires at least three devices to function.
questions.explanation: A network can be formed with as few as two devices.

questions.q: A network node can only be a computer or server.
questions.explanation: Nodes include printers, switches, routers, and IoT devices.

questions.q: A client can never act as a server.
questions.explanation: In peer-to-peer networks, a client can act as a server.

questions.q: A switch is used to connect different LANs.
questions.explanation: Routers connect different LANs; switches connect devices within a LAN.

questions.q: Routers have more network interfaces than switches.
questions.explanation: Switches typically have many more interfaces (ports) than routers.

questions.q: A firewall can be placed both inside and outside a network.
questions.explanation: True. Internal firewalls are used for segmentation.

questions.q: A Next-Generation Firewall has fewer features than a traditional firewall.
questions.explanation: NGFWs have significantly more features than traditional ones.

questions.q: A host-based firewall is a hardware device.
questions.explanation: Host-based firewalls are software applications installed on an OS.

questions.q: A switch operates at the Network layer (Layer 3).
questions.explanation: Standard switches operate at Layer 2 (Data Link).

questions.q: The China Telecom Data Center is located in Japan.
questions.explanation: It is located in China.

questions.q: Which attribute is used to set the style of an HTML element?
questions.explanation: The style attribute is used to apply inline styles, such as color, font, and size, directly to an HTML element [1], [2].

questions.q: Which property is used to define the background color for an HTML element?
questions.explanation: The background-color property defines the background color for an HTML element [3]. While 'bgcolor' was used as an attribute in older versions, 'background-color' is the CSS property used within a style attribute [4], [5].

questions.q: In HTML, which tag is used to define a hyperlink?
questions.explanation: Hyperlinks are defined with the <a> (anchor) tag [6], [2].

questions.q: What is the most important attribute of the <a> element, used to indicate the link's destination?
questions.explanation: The href attribute indicates the destination of the link [7], [8].

questions.q: Which attribute is used to open a linked document in a new browser window or tab?
questions.explanation: Setting the target attribute to '_blank' allows the browser to open the link in another page or tab [7], [9].

questions.q: True or False: A link can only be applied to text.
questions.explanation: False. A link does not have to be text; it can be an image or any other HTML element [10], [6].

questions.q: Which scheme should be used inside the href attribute to create a link that opens the user's email program?
questions.explanation: The mailto: scheme is used inside the href attribute to create an email link [11], [8].

questions.q: To create a bookmark and jump to a specific part of a page, which attribute must you first add to the target element?
questions.explanation: To make a bookmark, you must first create it using the id attribute on an element, and then link to it using href='#idName' [11], [12].

questions.q: What is a characteristic of the tag in HTML?
options: It is an empty tag and does not have a closing tag.

It must be used inside a

tag.
questions.explanation: The tag is empty, meaning it contains attributes only and does not have a closing tag [13].

questions.q: Which attribute is required for an tag to provide alternate text if the image cannot be displayed?
questions.explanation: The alt attribute is required and provides alternate text for an image [13], [14].

questions.q: What is the recommended method for defining the width and height of an image?
options: Using the style attribute with CSS properties
questions.explanation: It is recommended to use the style attribute for width and height to define the size of the image [13], [14].

questions.q: Which tag is used to define an unordered (bulleted) list?
questions.explanation: An unordered list is created using the <ul> tag [15], [16].

questions.q: Which tag is used to define a single list item within either an ordered or unordered list?
questions.explanation: Each list item starts with the <li> tag [16], [17].

questions.q: What is the default numbering scheme for an ordered list (<ol>)?
questions.explanation: By default, the numbering for an ordered list starts at one (1) and is incremented by one for each item [17], [18].

questions.q: In a description list (<dl>), which tag is used to define the term or name?
questions.explanation: The <dt> tag defines the term (name) in a description list, while <dd> describes each term [19], [20].

questions.q: Which attribute is used with the <ol> tag to specify the starting point of the numbering?
questions.explanation: The start attribute for the <ol> tag is used to specify the starting point of the numbering [21].

questions.q: Which tag is used to define the structure of an HTML document?
questions.explanation: All three tags are essential for HTML document structure: <html> wraps the entire document, <head> contains metadata, and <body> contains the visible content.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a type of cable used as a physical transmission medium?
questions.explanation: Wireless is a transmission medium but is not categorized as a cable [1].

questions.q: What does UTP stand for in networking?
questions.explanation: UTP stands for Unshielded Twisted Pair [1].

questions.q: What is the primary advantage of using fiber optic cables over copper cables?
questions.explanation: Fiber optic cables provide significantly higher bandwidth and speed than copper alternatives [1].

questions.q: Which of the following cables is typically used for Ethernet connections?
questions.explanation: Twisted pair is the standard cable type used for Ethernet connections [2].

questions.q: What type of cable is characterized by having a central conductor surrounded by insulation and a metallic shield?
questions.explanation: This describes the physical structure of a Coaxial cable [2].

questions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of STP cables?
options: They have shielding to reduce interference.
They are only used for short distances.
They are made of glass fibers.
questions.explanation: Shielded Twisted Pair (STP) uses a metallic shield to reduce electromagnetic interference [2].

questions.q: What is the purpose of a crossover cable?
options: To connect different types of networks
To increase the speed of data transmission
questions.explanation: Crossover cables are designed to connect two similar devices, such as two computers, directly to one another [3].

questions.q: Which type of cable is most commonly used in residential networking?
questions.explanation: Twisted pair cables are the most frequent choice for home and residential network setups [3].

questions.q: What is the main disadvantage of using twisted pair cables?
options: They are susceptible to electromagnetic interference.
questions.explanation: Twisted pair cables are vulnerable to electromagnetic interference (EMI) compared to other media [3, 4].

questions.q: What is the primary use of coaxial cables?
questions.explanation: Coaxial cables are primarily utilized for cable TV and high-speed internet connections [4].

questions.q: Which type of twisted pair cable is more effective at reducing electromagnetic interference?
questions.explanation: Because of its additional shielding, STP is more effective than UTP at reducing interference [4].

questions.q: Which of the following is a disadvantage of fiber optic cables?

questions.q: What type of cable is typically used for connecting a computer to a switch in a local area network (LAN)?

questions.q: Which type of cable is best suited for high-speed internet connections?

questions.q: What is the main reason for twisting the pairs of wires in twisted pair cables?
options: To make the cable more flexible
questions.explanation: Twisting the wires helps cancel out and reduce electromagnetic interference [5, 6].

questions.q: What is the main purpose of an operating system?
options: To make the computer easier to use
To manage computer hardware and software resources
questions.explanation: An OS manages resources, provides an interface, and makes the system user-friendly.

questions.q: The kernel is:
options: The core component that runs at all times
A temporary program loaded at startup
questions.explanation: The kernel is the one program running at all times on the computer.

questions.q: Which component of a computer system provides basic computing resources?
questions.explanation: Hardware (CPU, memory, I/O) provides the fundamental resources.

questions.q: What does DMA stand for?
questions.explanation: DMA allows high-speed I/O devices to transmit data directly to memory.

questions.q: Which storage device is typically volatile?
questions.explanation: RAM loses its contents when power is turned off.

questions.q: Multiprogramming is designed to:
questions.explanation: It keeps the CPU busy by always having a job to execute.

questions.q: In symmetric multiprocessing (SMP):
options: Only one processor can run the kernel
questions.explanation: In SMP, each processor performs all tasks including OS functions.

questions.q: What is the purpose of an interrupt vector?
options: To store the addresses of interrupt service routines
questions.explanation: It is an array of pointers to the specific routines that handle interrupts.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a function of process management?
questions.explanation: File compression is a file management or utility task, not a process management core task.

questions.q: Virtual memory allows:
options: Execution of processes not completely in memory
questions.explanation: It allows programs to run even if they are larger than physical memory.

questions.q: The bootstrap program is typically stored in:
questions.explanation: It is stored in firmware (ROM) so it is available immediately on power-up.

questions.q: Which of these is a real-time operating system characteristic?
questions.explanation: Real-time systems must process data and respond within fixed time constraints.

questions.q: In client-server computing, the server:
questions.explanation: The server waits for requests and provides data or services to clients.

questions.q: What is caching?
options: Storing data temporarily in faster storage
questions.explanation: Caching copies data to a faster storage system for quicker access.

questions.q: Which mode allows privileged instructions to execute?
questions.explanation: Privileged instructions can only run in kernel mode to protect the system.

questions.q: A trap is:
questions.explanation: A trap is caused by an error (like division by zero) or a user request for OS service.

questions.q: In a clustered system, high availability means:
questions.explanation: Clustered systems are designed so the service continues even if one node fails.

questions.q: Which is NOT a mass storage management activity?
questions.explanation: Compiler optimization is a development tool task, not a storage task.

questions.q: The mode bit is used to distinguish between:
questions.explanation: It indicates whether the CPU is running user code or kernel code.

questions.q: Open-source operating systems are characterized by:
questions.explanation: Open-source means the source code is public and can be modified by anyone.

questions.q: An operating system acts as an intermediary between users and hardware.
questions.explanation: This is the fundamental definition of an OS.

questions.q: Application programs directly control hardware without OS intervention.
questions.explanation: Applications must use the OS to access hardware resources safely.

questions.q: The kernel is the first program loaded when a computer starts.
questions.explanation: The bootstrap program loads first, which then loads the kernel.

questions.q: All operating systems have the same definition and components.
questions.explanation: Definitions vary; some include GUI/apps, others only the kernel.

questions.q: I/O devices and CPU can execute concurrently.
questions.explanation: Device controllers and the CPU work at the same time to increase efficiency.

questions.q: Main memory is typically non-volatile.
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile; it loses data when power is lost.

questions.q: Secondary storage is faster than main memory.
questions.explanation: Secondary storage (like HDDs) is much slower than RAM.

questions.q: Multiprocessor systems always have better performance than single processor systems.
questions.explanation: Performance depends on the application and overhead; it's not 'always' better.

questions.q: In asymmetric multiprocessing, all processors are equal.
questions.explanation: In asymmetric, one processor is the master and others follow instructions.

questions.q: Clustered systems share storage via a common bus.
questions.explanation: They usually share storage via a Storage Area Network (SAN).

questions.q: Timesharing systems require response time less than 1 second.
questions.explanation: Timesharing (multitasking) needs fast response to appear interactive.

questions.q: A program and a process are the same thing.
questions.explanation: A program is passive (file on disk); a process is active (executing).

questions.q: Multi-threaded processes have multiple program counters.
questions.explanation: Each thread in a process has its own program counter.

questions.q: Virtual memory eliminates the need for secondary storage.
questions.explanation: Virtual memory actually relies on secondary storage to store overflow data.

questions.q: File systems abstract physical storage properties into logical files.
questions.explanation: The OS hides disk hardware details and presents a file-based view.

questions.q: All storage devices need to be managed for optimal performance.
questions.explanation: Management (scheduling/allocation) is key for system speed.

questions.q: Protection and security refer to the same concept in operating systems.
questions.explanation: Protection is internal (between users/processes); Security is external defense.

questions.q: Distributed systems must use identical hardware components.
questions.explanation: Distributed systems are often heterogeneous (mixed hardware).

questions.q: Real-time systems prioritize meeting deadlines over throughput.
questions.explanation: Meeting time constraints is more important than the amount of work finished.

questions.q: Handheld systems have the same requirements as desktop systems.
questions.explanation: Handhelds have limited power, memory, and screen size.

questions.q: Peer-to-peer systems distinguish clearly between clients and servers.
questions.explanation: In P2P, nodes can act as both clients and servers.

questions.q: Web-based computing has made operating systems less important.
questions.explanation: The OS is still vital for managing the hardware the browser runs on.

questions.q: All operating system code runs in kernel mode.
questions.explanation: Some OS components (like system programs) run in user mode.

questions.q: System calls always return control to the user program immediately.
questions.explanation: Some calls must wait for slow I/O operations to finish first.

questions.q: A device controller has its own local buffer.
questions.explanation: Controllers use buffers to store data before moving it to memory.

questions.q: Polling is more efficient than interrupts for I/O handling.
questions.explanation: Interrupts are more efficient because the CPU doesn't waste time waiting/checking.

questions.q: DMA reduces the number of interrupts during data transfer.
questions.explanation: DMA sends one interrupt per block of data rather than per byte.

questions.q: Cache coherency is only important in single processor systems.
questions.explanation: Coherency is vital in multiprocessors so all CPUs see the same data.

questions.q: Spooling allows overlapping of input and output operations.
questions.explanation: Spooling stands for Simultaneous Peripheral Operations Online.

questions.q: User IDs are used for access control in operating systems.
questions.explanation: The OS uses IDs to determine what files or programs a user can access.

questions.q: What is the contrapositive of 'If it rains, then the grass is wet'?
options: If the grass is wet, then it rains
If it doesn't rain, then the grass is not wet
If the grass is not wet, then it doesn't rain
If it rains, then the grass is not wet
questions.explanation: The contrapositive of 'if p then q' is 'if not q then not p'. Therefore, 'If the grass is not wet, then it does not rain'.

questions.q: What is the negation of the statement 'All cats are black'?
questions.explanation: The negation of a universal statement (All) is an existential statement (Some ... not).

questions.q: Let P(x) be 'x is a prime number' and Q(x) be 'x is odd.' Which statement represents 'All prime numbers except 2 are odd'?
options: For all x(P(x) implies Q(x)) or x=2
For all x((P(x) and x is not 2) implies Q(x))
questions.explanation: The expression targets all x that are both prime and not equal to 2.

questions.q: Which of these statements about logical equivalences is FALSE?
options: p implies q is equivalent to not p or q
not(p implies q) is equivalent to p and not q
p implies q is equivalent to not q implies not p
p implies (q implies r) is equivalent to (p implies q) implies r
questions.explanation: Implication is not associative; changing the grouping changes the meaning of the statement.

questions.q: If P(x) means 'x is a dog' and Q(x) means 'x has four legs', which statement means 'All dogs have four legs'?
options: There exists an x such that (P(x) and Q(x))
There exists an x such that (P(x) implies Q(x))
questions.explanation: Universal statements regarding properties are represented as 'For all x, if x is P, then x is Q'.

questions.q: If P(x) means 'x is a student' and Q(x) means 'x studies hard', what does 'There exists an x such that (P(x) and Q(x))' mean in English?
questions.explanation: The existential quantifier translates to 'There exists' or 'Some'.

questions.q: Let P(x,y) mean 'x is greater than y'. What is the meaning of 'For all x, there exists a y such that P(x,y)'?
options: For every x, there is some y that is greater than x
For every x, there is some y that x is greater than
There exists an x that is greater than all y
There exists a y that is greater than all x
questions.explanation: This means that for every chosen x, you can find at least one y that is smaller than it.

questions.q: The contrapositive of 'If n is even, then n squared is even' is:
options: If n is odd, then n squared is odd
If n squared is odd, then n is odd
If n is not even, then n squared is not even
If n squared is not even, then n is not even
questions.explanation: We negate and swap both sides: 'If n squared is not even, then n is not even'.

questions.q: What is the symbolic form of 'Not all doctors work in hospitals'?
options: For all x(Doctor(x) implies not Hospital(x))
There exists an x such that (Doctor(x) and not Hospital(x))
It is not the case that for all x(Doctor(x) implies Hospital(x))
questions.explanation: Saying 'Not all' is logically the same as saying 'There is at least one that is not'.

questions.q: If C(x) means 'x is a car' and F(x) means 'x is fast', which symbolizes 'Only fast vehicles are cars'?
options: For all x(Car(x) if and only if Fast(x))
There exists an x such that (Car(x) and Fast(x))
questions.explanation: The phrase 'Only B are A' means that if something is an A, it must be a B.

questions.q: If f(x) = x cubed minus 3x and g(x) = x + 2, then (f composed with g)(1) equals:
questions.explanation: First find g(1) = 3. Then find f(3) = 3 cubed (27) minus 3 times 3 (9), which equals 18.

questions.q: For which function is the inverse of f equal to f?
questions.explanation: A function that is its own inverse is an involution. For f(x)=1/x, f(f(x)) = 1/(1/x) = x.

questions.q: The power set of {a, b} contains:
questions.explanation: The number of elements in a power set is 2 raised to the power of the number of elements in the set. 2 squared is 4.

questions.q: Let A = {1, 2, 3} and B = {2, 3, 4}. What is (A minus B) union (B minus A)?
questions.explanation: A minus B leaves {1}. B minus A leaves {4}. Combining them gives {1, 4}.

questions.explanation: By definition, $P(A|B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}$. Since $A \subset B$, the intersection $A \cap B = A$. Therefore, $P(A|B) = \frac{P(A)}{P(B)}$. None of the first three options match this result.

questions.q:
Consider the following information:

| Volume of sales (units) | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 | 10 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Total expenses ($) | 74 | 77 | 82 | 86 | 92 | 95 |

- $a)$ Find the least-squares line for the data.
questions.answer:
Let $x$ be the volume and $y$ be the expenses. Calculations: $n=6, \sum x = 45, \sum y = 506, \sum x^2 = 355, \sum xy = 3872$.
Slope $b = \frac{n\sum xy - \sum x \sum y}{n\sum x^2 - (\sum x)^2} = \frac{6(3872) - 45(506)}{6(355) - (45)^2} = \frac{462}{105} = 4.4$.
Intercept $a = \bar{y} - b\bar{x} = \frac{506}{6} - 4.4(\frac{45}{6}) = 84.333 - 33 = 51.333$.
Least-squares line: $\hat{y} = 51.333 + 4.4x$.
questions.explanation: The least-squares line $\hat{y} = a + bx$ is calculated using the standard formulas for regression coefficients. The intercept $a$ can be represented as the fraction $\frac{154}{3}$.

questions.q: A code consists of a digit chosen from 0 to 7 followed by a letter of the alphabet. What is the probability the code is 7Z?
questions.explanation: Digits available: 0–7 → 8 choices. Letters: 26 choices. Total outcomes = $8 \times 26 = 208$. Only one outcome is '7Z', so $P(\text{7Z}) = \dfrac{1}{208}$.

questions.q: If $A$ and $B$ are two independent events such that $P(A) > 0$ and $P(B) \neq 1$, then $P(B^c \mid A^c)$ is equal to:
questions.explanation:
Since $A$ and $B$ are independent, $A^c$ and $B^c$ are also independent. Therefore:
$$P(B^c \mid A^c) = P(B^c) = 1 - P(B)$$

questions.q: If $A$ and $B$ are independent events, then $P(B \mid A) =$
questions.explanation:
By definition of independence: $P(A \cap B) = P(A) \cdot P(B)$.
$$P(B \mid A) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(A)} = \frac{P(A) \cdot P(B)}{P(A)} = P(B)$$

questions.q: If $A \subset B$, then $P(B \mid A) =$
questions.explanation:
If $A \subset B$, then $A \cap B = A$. Therefore:
$$P(B \mid A) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(A)} = \frac{P(A)}{P(A)} = 1$$
Since none of the listed options equals 1 in general, the answer is **None of them**.

questions.q: If the knowledge that an event $A$ has occurred implies that a second event $B$ **cannot** occur, the events $A$ and $B$ are said to be:
questions.explanation: Mutually exclusive events cannot occur simultaneously. If knowing $A$ occurred means $B$ cannot occur, then $A \cap B = \emptyset$, which is the definition of mutual exclusivity.

questions.q:
A process has two quality checks:

- Check 2 passes with probability **0.90** (given Check 1 passes)

What's the probability that a product passes **both** checks?

Using the multiplication rule:

A mobile device attempts to connect to a Wi-Fi network **10 times** during a commute. Each attempt has a **0.70** probability of success.

**(a)** What is the probability of **fewer than 6** successful connections?

**(b)** Calculate the **standard deviation**.
questions.answer:
Given: $n = 10,\ p = 0.7,\ q = 0.3$. This is a **Binomial distribution** $X \sim B(n, p)$.

**Formula:** $P(X = x) = \binom{n}{x} p^x q^{n-x}$

**(a) $P(X < 6)$:**

$$P(X < 6) = \sum_{x=0}^{5} \binom{10}{x}(0.7)^x(0.3)^{10-x}$$

| $x$ | $P(X=x)$ |
|---|---|
| 0 | $\approx 0.000006$ |
| 1 | $\approx 0.000138$ |
| 2 | $\approx 0.001447$ |
| 3 | $\approx 0.009001$ |
| 4 | $\approx 0.036757$ |
| 5 | $\approx 0.102919$ |
| **Total** | $\approx 0.1503$ |

$$\boxed{P(X < 6) \approx 0.1503}$$

**(b) Standard Deviation:**

$$SD = \sqrt{n \cdot p \cdot q} = \sqrt{10 \times 0.7 \times 0.3} = \sqrt{2.1} \approx 1.449$$
questions.explanation: For a binomial distribution $B(n,p)$: mean $\mu = np$, variance $\sigma^2 = npq$, and $SD = \sqrt{npq}$.

questions.q: If the average of a series of values is 10 and their variance is 9, then the **coefficient of variation** is:
questions.explanation:
$$SD = \sqrt{\text{Variance}} = \sqrt{9} = 3$$
$$CV = \frac{SD}{\bar{x}} \times 100 = \frac{3}{10} \times 100 = 30\%$$

questions.q: If the standard deviation of a set of observations is **6** and each observation is **divided by 6**, the standard deviation of the new set of observations will be:
questions.explanation:
When all observations are divided by a constant $c$, the standard deviation is also divided by $c$:
$$SD_{\text{new}} = \frac{SD}{c} = \frac{6}{6} = 1$$

questions.q:

The value 400 is an extreme outlier. The **mean** would be heavily skewed by it. The **median** is resistant to outliers and best represents the center of this dataset.

$$\text{Median} = 30 \quad (\text{4th value in sorted order})$$

questions.q: In meteorology, the intensity of UV-B radiation is classified as: *weak, moderate, strong, extreme*. What is the **best measure** for this data?
questions.explanation: This is **ordinal categorical** data (categories with a defined order but no numeric values). The **Mode** is the most appropriate measure of central tendency since arithmetic operations (mean, median) are not meaningful on categorical labels.

questions.q: If $\sum x_i = 20$ and $\bar{x} = 2$, then the **rank of the Median** is:
questions.explanation:
First find $n$:
$$\bar{x} = \frac{\sum x_i}{n} \Rightarrow n = \frac{\sum x_i}{\bar{x}} = \frac{20}{2} = 10$$

Rank of the Median for even $n$:
$$\text{Median rank} = \frac{n}{2} \text{ and } \frac{n}{2}+1 = \text{5th and 6th values} \Rightarrow \text{rank } = 5.5$$

questions.q: Which rule of inference is used to derive the conclusion q ∨ r from the premises p ∨ q and ¬p ∨ r?
questions.explanation: Resolution takes two clauses with a literal and its negation to produce a new clause.

questions.q: Given the premises: ∀x(P(x) → Q(x)), P(c) for an arbitrary element c. What rule justifies the conclusion Q(c)?
options: Universal Instantiation followed by Modus Ponens
questions.explanation: First, you remove the 'for all' (Universal Instantiation) to get P(c) → Q(c), then apply Modus Ponens with P(c).

questions.q: What valid conclusion can be drawn from: (p ∧ q) → r and ¬r?
questions.explanation: By Modus Tollens, we get ¬(p ∧ q). By De Morgan's law, this is ¬p ∨ ¬q.

questions.q: Analyze the logical steps: 1. ∀x(P(x) → Q(x)), 2. ¬Q(a), 3. P(a) → Q(a) [Rule X], 4. ¬P(a) [Rule Y]. Identify Rule X and Rule Y.
options: X: Universal Generalization, Y: Modus Ponens
X: Universal Instantiation, Y: Modus Tollens
X: Existential Instantiation, Y: Modus Tollens
X: Universal Instantiation, Y: Disjunctive Syllogism
questions.explanation: X removes the quantifier for specific case 'a', and Y uses the negative conclusion to negate the premise.

questions.q: A detective reasons: 'If the butler committed the crime, then he was in the mansion at midnight. The butler was NOT in the mansion at midnight. Therefore, the butler did not commit the crime.' Which rule of inference is the detective using?
questions.explanation: If P then Q. Not Q. Therefore not P. This is Modus Tollens.

questions.q: To prove the statement 'For all integers n, if n² is odd, then n is odd' using Proof by Contraposition, what is the correct initial assumption?
options: Assume n is odd and n² is even
questions.explanation: Contraposition assumes the negation of the conclusion (n is not odd, so n is even) to prove the negation of the hypothesis.

questions.q: Identify the logical structure of the following proof attempt for the statement (P ∧ Q) → R: 'Suppose ¬R is true. We demonstrate that this implies ¬P ∨ ¬Q.'
questions.explanation: It assumes ¬Conclusion and derives ¬Hypothesis, which is the definition of contraposition.

questions.explanation: 'Only A are B' translates to 'If B, then A'. Here, if it is a car, it must be fast.

questions.explanation: This specifies that if a number is prime and is not 2, then it must be odd.

questions.q: Which of the following describes 'Data' according to the information concepts hierarchy?
options: Knowledge that has an evaluative component
Raw facts with no contextual meaning
questions.explanation: According to the sources, **Data** represents raw facts, while **Information** is processed data with contextual meaning that tells us 'who', 'what', 'where', and 'when'.

questions.q: The 'economical' characteristic of valuable information means it is expensive to produce.
questions.explanation: Information being **economical** means it should be **cost-effective to produce**, meaning its value should exceed the cost of producing it, rather than simply being expensive.

questions.q: During which phase of the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) is logical work converted into physical designs such as database and UI/UX designs?
questions.explanation: In the **Design** phase, architects and designers map requirements to architecture, database, UI/UX, and API designs, converting the **logical into the physical**.

questions.q: According to Agile values, what is prioritized over 'following a plan'?
questions.explanation: The Agile manifesto prioritizes **responding to change** over following a plan, as well as prioritizing individuals/interactions, working software, and customer collaboration over their traditional counterparts.

questions.q: Which method of valuing Information Systems involves doing things 'better' by transforming raw data into meaningful insights for decision-making?
questions.explanation: **Informating** refers to generating and publishing information throughout the organization to provide insights, whereas **Automating** focuses on doing things faster and **Strategizing** focuses on doing things smarter.

questions.q: E-business is narrower in scope than E-commerce because it only focuses on online transactions.
questions.explanation: False. **E-business** is broader because it encompasses all business activities conducted online, including **internal operations** like CRM and ERP, whereas **E-commerce** specifically focuses on digitally enabled commercial transactions between organizations and individuals.

questions.q: Which security threat involves a hacker trying to guess a password by automatically trying every possible combination until one works?
questions.explanation: A **Brute Force Attack** occurs when a hacker uses automated tools to guess a password or encryption key by trying every possible combination.

questions.q: A Context Diagram, the highest level of a Data Flow Diagram (DFD), should always show the internal Data Stores of the system.
questions.explanation: False. A **Context Diagram** defines system scope and boundary; it typically shows only one process and external entities, but **does not show Data Stores**, which are considered internal to the system.

questions.q: In the Three-Schema Architecture, which layer describes 'what' data is stored in the database and the relationships among that data while hiding physical storage details?
questions.explanation: The **Conceptual Layer** describes the community view of the database (entities and relationships), while the **Internal Layer** handles physical storage and the **External Layer** provides specific views for different users.

questions.q: Which cardinality ratio describes a relationship where an entity in A is associated with any number of entities in B, but an entity in B is associated with at most one entity in A?
questions.explanation: This describes a **One-to-Many (1:N)** relationship. An example provided in the sources is a Department having multiple Employees.
